Getting Started on Your Final Project

November 19, 2026

The Final Project 🎯

Two tracks


Shiny app 🧭

  • An interactive tool that lets a user explore data
  • The controls should teach the user something
  • Published on Posit Connect Cloud

Report 📝

  • A polished report written in Quarto
  • Built around at least one well-crafted visualization
  • Also published on Posit Connect Cloud


Same proposal, same studio sessions, same deadlines. See the Project Description.

What makes for a good project?


  • A clear question your audience can explore
  • Data that is comprehensive and convenient (no time for original data collection!)
  • At least one well-crafted, labeled visualization
  • App: controls that change the output in a way that teaches something
  • Report: writing that puts the visualization to work

Groups


  • Work alone or in a group of up to three
  • One proposal and one project per group; everyone shares the grade
  • Divide the work clearly (data wrangling, UI, server logic, writing…)
  • Include a short division-of-work note with your proposal and your final submission

The proposal


Four questions, a paragraph or two each:

  1. Question & track: What should your audience learn? App or report, and why? Link to examples you like.
  2. Data: What sources, variables, units and years? How will you merge?
  3. Visualization: What will they see, and what should they notice?
  4. Interactivity or narrative: What will the user control (app), or how is the report structured (report)?

Submit your unrendered .qmd on Blackboard.

Where to find data


  • Data we have used in class: V-Dem, World Bank (WDI), FRED, UCDP…
  • The Datasets page has many more
  • Pick something you can load into R today
  • If it needs an API key, plan to download once and save to a file

Scope it small 🔬


  • Start with a proof of concept: one or two indicators, one chart
  • Get that working before adding more data, inputs or sections
  • A simple project that works beats an ambitious one that doesn’t
  • You can always add more later

AI and your project


  • A full AI-assisted workflow is encouraged for the final project
  • But the design, data choices, analysis and interpretation must be yours
  • You should be able to explain and defend everything in your project
  • Note how you used AI in your final submission

Let’s Get Started 🛠️

Today’s plan

  1. Pick a track and form your group (10 min)
  2. Browse examples: the Shiny gallery, Our World in Data, apps from Shiny Basics and Advanced Shiny
  3. Find your data and load it into R—try a first glimpse() and a quick plot
  4. Start drafting your proposal


I’ll come around to talk through ideas with each person or group.
